question:
A 24-year-old female seeks contraceptive counseling at a clinic. She is on day 12 of her menstrual
cycle. Her medical history includes Wilson disease, hypertension, and constipation-predominant
irritable bowel syndrome. Current medications include trientine, hydrochlorothiazide, and polyethylene
glycol. Physical examination reveals a blood pressure of 133/95 mm Hg with normal cardiac and
pulmonary findings. Pregnancy test is negative. Which contraceptive option would be most appropriate
for this patient, considering minimal impact on blood pressure? Answer Choices: (A) Etonogestrel
implant (B) Norethindrone (C) Levonorgestrel-releasing IUD (D) Depot medroxyprogesterone acetate
injection (E) Vaginal contraceptive ring (F) Copper IUD (G) Progestin-only oral contraceptive pills (H)
Combined oral contraceptive pills (I) Hormonal patch (J) High-dose combined injectable contraceptives
 A. Combined oral contraceptive pills
B. High-dose combined injectable contraceptives
C. Levonorgestrel-releasing IUD
D. Vaginal contraceptive ring
E. Etonogestrel implant
F. Norethindrone
G. Hormonal patch
H. Depot medroxyprogesterone acetate injection
I. Progestin-only oral contraceptive pills
J. Copper IUD
